job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: The Harappan civilization was a remarkable urban society, but it was not uniform across all regions. While cities like Mohenjodaro featured a distinct Citadel and a Lower Town, other settlements like Dholavira were divided into three parts, each protected by massive stone walls. These cities were not military forts; instead, the Citadel served as a center for public rituals and administration. For instance, the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro was a specially lined tank used for sacred ritual bathing, not for recreational swimming. The Harappans were master builders who used baked bricks to construct durable, multi-room houses, far superior to simple mud structures. Their economy relied on trade, and they used stone seals to mark goods, acting like a stamp for ownership rather than currency for daily shopping. Despite their advanced technology, they did not use iron, relying instead on bronze and copper for their tools. The decline of these cities was not caused by a single war or sudden plague. Instead, it was a gradual process involving climate change, the drying up of rivers, and the shifting of trade routes. As urban life faded, the people did not vanish; they migrated to smaller settlements, carrying their traditions and knowledge into the future.

items.evidence: While cities like Mohenjodaro featured a distinct Citadel and a Lower Town, other settlements like Dholavira were divided into three parts, each protected by massive stone walls.
items.q: How was the city of Dholavira planned differently from Mohenjodaro?
options: It was split into three walled parts
It had just a Citadel and Lower Town
It was a walled fort built for wars
It had one part with thin mud walls
items.explain: Mohenjodaro had two parts, but Dholavira had three parts, each protected by massive stone walls.

wrong.why: thinks all Harappan cities had only two parts
thinks walled cities were military forts
thinks Harappans built only weak mud structures

items.evidence: For instance, the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro was a specially lined tank used for sacred ritual bathing, not for recreational swimming.
items.q: Why did the people of Mohenjodaro build the Great Bath?
options: For holy washing during religious ceremonies
For people to swim and have fun
For soldiers to train for battle
For storing drinking water for the city
items.explain: The Great Bath was a lined tank for sacred ritual bathing, not for swimming for fun.

wrong.why: thinks the Great Bath was a swimming pool
thinks the Citadel was used for war
guesses that any tank must store water

items.evidence: Their economy relied on trade, and they used stone seals to mark goods, acting like a stamp for ownership rather than currency for daily shopping.
items.q: A Harappan trader presses a seal onto a sack of grain. What does the mark show?
options: That the goods belong to a certain owner
That the seal was given as a coin
That the grain is ready for daily shopping
That a king wrote a record about it
items.explain: Seals marked goods like a stamp showing ownership; they were not money for shopping.

wrong.why: thinks seals were used as coins
grabs the phrase 'daily shopping' from the passage
thinks we have writings by Harappan kings

items.evidence: Despite their advanced technology, they did not use iron, relying instead on bronze and copper for their tools.
items.q: An archaeologist digs up a Harappan tool. What metal is it most likely made of?
options: Bronze or copper
Iron, since they were advanced
Iron mixed with some copper
Gold, since they were rich
items.explain: The Harappans did not use iron; they made their tools from bronze and copper.

wrong.why: thinks advanced people must have used iron
mixes the correct metal with iron
links a rich trading society with gold tools

items.evidence: Instead, it was a gradual process involving climate change, the drying up of rivers, and the shifting of trade routes.
items.q: Which best explains why the Harappan cities slowly became empty?
options: Rivers dried up and trade routes moved
One big war destroyed every city
All the people suddenly died out
A sudden plague spread through the towns
items.explain: The decline was gradual, caused by climate change, drying rivers and shifting trade routes.

wrong.why: thinks a single war ended the civilisation
thinks all Harappan people died out
picks the plague the passage rules out
